ONE SMALL CHANGE AT A TIME

Let’s find your clarinet sound.

Choose what you hear. Try one change, play again, and listen with your teacher. These tips are starting points; your teacher can help find what works for you.

Still stuck? Ask your teacher to check your setup and instrument. Sometimes the instrument needs a little help, too.
LET’S GET IT WORKING

Instrument troubleshooting

Choose your instrument above, then find what is happening. The label shows where to start.

Student check

A simple routine your teacher has already shown you.

Teacher first

Ask your teacher to inspect it and decide what to do.

Repair assessment

Have your teacher arrange a qualified instrument technician.

If something will not move, do not force it. Student checks are only for familiar routines. If you are unsure, ask your teacher first.

Before it goes to the shop

Tell your teacher when the problem started, which notes or parts are affected, and whether it followed a fall, cleaning, or assembly. Keep any loose pieces. A teacher can handle routine care they are trained to do and help decide whether repair is needed.

For school-owned or rented instruments, let your teacher or family contact the school or rental provider first. Follow the care instructions for your actual model.

THE TEACHER’S MUSIC ROOM

Beginning Band Board

Seven instruments. Seven notes. One shared musical language.

Do = concert B♭. Written notes and registers follow the supplied beginning-band chart. Euphonium uses bass clef. Low Ti is the leading tone immediately below Do.

Original fingerings and shapes come directly from your supplied PDF. The added low Ti and La figures reuse its artwork and match its style. Bell-kit bars follow the reference layout; the selected bar is outlined in gold.

Hear it plays a reference tone at the sounding pitch. It is a pitch guide, not a recorded example of instrument tone. Bell-kit audio sounds two octaves above its written notes.

Pen, touch, and mouse drawing are supported. Use Pen only if your display identifies its stylus separately from touch; otherwise leave it off. Drawings are saved in this browser on this device.

Open the original five-note charts ↗

Rhythm Writer has a reusable shelf of notes, rests, and measure lines. Drag out any number of copies, or tap a symbol to add it. Select a copy to move, duplicate, or delete it. Undo also restores a cleared rhythm.

Clefs and rhythm symbols use Bravura notation by Steinberg Media Technologies, under the SIL Open Font License.

Fingering references

    Sound Help offers practical starting points. Troubleshooting separates familiar student checks, teacher assistance, and professional repair. Sources appear with the relevant guidance; use the care instructions for your own instrument model.
